text:
Source-assisted reading of F-53hg (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 120). Reread on the native images by a research reader: canvas 1, lines 2-12 and 14-24; canvas 0, the last two lines. Read before any source was known (in the image-only first reading): on canvas 1 "medici", "intellegendo mo", "humore", "quod sit malagma proinde", "dicantur malactica", "sebum deinde taurinum", "De adipibus", "inter quadrupedes", "ualde melius est leopardinum quam leoninum", "& melius est ursinum quam taurinum", "uero spissius & siccius & magis hir", "obtimum est adipe anserin"; on canvas 0 "quodam sed spisso". Canvas 1 lines 2-12 were corrected with the Venice 1522 text of Galen, Ad Glauconem II, open beside the image; the three lines from the middle of canvas 0 were read only with that text as a guide; in canvas 1 line 2 the words "inde modo aut uix" follow Vendome, Bibliotheque municipale, Ms. 109. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels. Parentheses expand abbreviations; [..] marks letters lost or not read; (?) marks an uncertain reading. Everything not listed here rests on the image-only first reading.
